clue.text: Nobleman and king left to the end

indicators.note: the left-hand letter of the king's name is shifted along to the end of the word

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king, the most famous king in crosswords

explanation.surface: A list of aristocrats: a nobleman and a king, with the king left until last.
explanation.walkthrough: The L of LEAR, not the abbreviation for left, is what moves; 'and' simply joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British peer ranking between a marquess and a viscount.

clue.text: America brought in wise folk to identify a string of items

indicators.note: the wise folk take the country's abbreviation into their midst

parts.note: sages are wise people

explanation.surface: The US recruited wise people to help identify some items in a series.
explanation.definitionFit: Butchers' links of sausages come joined in a chain, so the answer is a familiar example of a string of things.

clue.text: Bright item's endless glare

indicators.note: the word for the glare loses its final letter

parts.note: to glare is to stare angrily, so the noun stare fits

explanation.surface: A shiny object gives off a glare that never ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a shining body in the night sky, an obvious example of something bright.

clue.text: Current obligation to adopt tax move

parts.note: AC is alternating current

indicators.note: the obligation takes the tax inside itself, as a family takes in a child

parts.note: a tie is something that binds you, an obligation
VAT is value added tax, the UK sales tax

explanation.surface: A financial bulletin: a current commitment to take on a tax measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move' reads as a noun at the end of the surface, but it is the verb meaning to set going.
explanation.definitionFit: To activate something is to set it in motion, to start it working.

clue.text: Cold current picked up speed, rising to frozen region

indicators.note: in a down entry, picking up the letters lifts them so they read bottom to top

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: the word for speed climbs the down entry, so it reads upwards

parts.note: pace is rate of movement

explanation.surface: A weather report: a cold current gathered speed as it rose towards a frozen area.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice cap is a permanent covering of ice over a polar or mountainous area of land.

clue.text: Maintain opinion on vehicle opponent rolled

parts.note: someone's take on a matter is their view
a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: the opponent is turned over, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a foe is an enemy or opponent

explanation.surface: Someone holds a view about a car whose rival overturned.
explanation.definitionFit: To take care of something is to look after it and keep it in good order.

clue.text: Old way to bring in a government rebellion, initially a boost for a member?

indicators.note: the old way opens up to admit the three initial letters inside it

parts.note: a via was a Roman road, an ancient way

indicators.note: only the opening letters of the three words are taken

parts.note: the first letters of these three words are the ones taken

explanation.surface: An outdated method to bring in a government revolt, then a pick-me-up for an MP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' looks like a member of parliament after all the government talk; it is the male member.
explanation.definitionFit: The drug treats erectile dysfunction, so it gives a cheeky lift to that part of the body.

clue.text: Instinctive to limit large surplus production

indicators.note: the instinctive word surrounds and so confines the size letter

parts.note: a gut reaction is an instinctive one

explanation.surface: An instinct to restrict large-scale overproduction.
explanation.definitionFit: A glut is an oversupply, more goods produced than the market wants.

clue.text: First carriage returned in a different place

parts.note: A is top grade, first class, as in A1

indicators.note: the carriage comes back the other way, read right to left

parts.note: a trap is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage

explanation.surface: The leading carriage was sent back to a different spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Things set apart are separated, each in a different location from the other.

clue.text: Draw in to prepare to shoot a lake bird

indicators.note: the draw sits inside the other letters

parts.note: to cock a gun is to raise its hammer ready to fire
taken as written
a tie is a drawn game

explanation.surface: A hunter is drawn into getting ready to shoot a waterbird on a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockatiel is a small crested Australian parrot, popular as a pet.

clue.text: Boy is caught capturing series — on this?

indicators.note: the boy holds the series abbreviation inside him

parts.note: a lad is a boy
taken as written
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A boy is caught recording a TV series, and the question asks what he recorded it on.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points back at the series: the series might be stored on one of these.
explanation.definitionFit: A laserdisc was an optical video disc format of the 1980s on which films and programmes were sold.

clue.text: Article about government issue recalled quantity

indicators.note: the whole assembly is called back, so it reads in reverse
the article goes round the government issue

parts.note: the is the definite article
GI originally stood for government issue

explanation.surface: A report on a recalled batch of government-issued goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight is a number, and a number is a count or amount of things.

clue.text: Leave sextet enthralled by the main guitarist

indicators.note: the leaving and the six are held captive within the sea

parts.note: the main is the open sea in old poetic usage
to go is to leave
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Six musicians quit, spellbound by the great classical guitarist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' looks like 'the principal' but is the old word for the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrés Segovia was the Spanish virtuoso who made the classical guitar a concert instrument.

clue.text: Touches up, cuddling male character

indicators.note: the reversed touches wrap around the male letter
in a down entry the touches are written upwards

parts.note: pats are light touches

explanation.surface: Someone gives a male character little touches while hugging him.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of a certain stamp is of a certain kind or nature, so stamp means character.

clue.text: Archdeacon attending hospital department getting warning about a couple of veins

parts.note: Ven, for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon
A&E is the accident and emergency department

indicators.note: about means around, so the warning surrounds the letter

parts.note: cave, Latin for 'beware', is a schoolboy warning

explanation.surface: A senior cleric at the emergency department is warned about a pair of blood vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: CAVE (pronounced kay-vee) was a schoolboy cry of 'look out'. The plural venae cavae are the two large veins carrying blood to the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: The venae cavae are the two great veins, superior and inferior, returning blood to the heart.

clue.text: Calm, being about to enter horse race

indicators.note: the abbreviation for about goes into the race

parts.note: a plate is a race with a prize, as in the Queen's Plate
ca, circa, means about

explanation.surface: Someone stays calm when about to ride in a horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: To placate is to soothe or pacify someone who is angry.

clue.text: Carefully consider status of the king of the country of the blind?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to look over closely and appraisingly

definitions.text: status of the king of the country of the blind
definitions.meaning: second meaning, playful: the proverb says in the country of the blind the one-eyed man is king

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning stretches the phrase to 'one eye up', the one-eyed king's advantage over his blind subjects.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye up a thing or person is to look at them carefully, sizing them up.

clue.text: Each is discounted in a motive for crime

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the letters for each are knocked off the motive, as a discount knocks off price

parts.note: a reason is a motive

explanation.surface: Each person's share is reduced, which becomes a motive for a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the criminal act of deliberately setting fire to property.

clue.text: A few backtracked, eliminating zero spaces in printed material

indicators.note: the letter for zero is removed
the word goes back on itself, read right to left

parts.note: some means a few

explanation.surface: A few people retreated, cutting out the zero spaces in a printed document.
explanation.definitionFit: An em is a printer's unit of measurement, so em spaces separate text in typesetting.

clue.text: Travelling illegally, drag American through control

definitions.note: used adjectivally, as in a stowaway passenger

indicators.note: the dragging and the American pass right through the control word

parts.note: sway means power or rule, as in hold sway
to tow is to drag

explanation.surface: An American is dragged through passport control for travelling without a ticket.
explanation.definitionFit: A stowaway hides aboard a ship or plane to make a journey without paying.

clue.text: Silver luminance seen in wings of exquisite bird

indicators.note: the silver and luminance appear between those wings
the outer letters of the word, its two edges like a pair of wings

parts.note: only its first and last letters are used, the two wings
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
L is the physics symbol for luminance

explanation.surface: A silvery sheen glints on the wings of a beautiful bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The eagle is a large bird of prey with broad wings and a hooked bill.

clue.text: Most of shop opened by key that's cut? Serious stuff

indicators.note: the shortened informing word is split open to take in the cut key word
all but the last letter of the informing word is used

parts.note: to shop or grass someone is to inform on them to the police

indicators.note: the key word is trimmed of its last letter

parts.note: vital means crucial, key

explanation.surface: A shop is broken into by someone with a cut key, a grave matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shop' is the verb, British slang for betraying to the police, not a store.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravitas is dignity and seriousness of manner, weightiness in a person or occasion.

clue.text: Invention having soft (not loud) colour

indicators.note: the invention takes on the soft letter
the loud letter is dropped in its favour, the soft replacing it

parts.note: a figment is something invented by the mind

explanation.surface: A new product with a soft rather than loud shade.
explanation.walkthrough: In music p (piano) is soft and f (forte) is loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigment is a substance that gives colour, as in paints and dyes.

clue.text: Instruction to depart for one uppity solicitor

indicators.note: in a down entry, uppity has the letters going up, read in reverse

parts.note: eg means for example, for one
a tout solicits custom, pestering people to buy

explanation.surface: An order to leave given to one arrogant lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' suggests a British lawyer; here it is anyone who solicits.
explanation.definitionFit: Get out! is a blunt command telling someone to go away.

clue.text: Island extremely welcoming to some game

indicators.note: the extreme word takes the hunter's haul inside it

parts.note: too means excessively, to an extreme
a bag is the quantity of game a hunter shoots

explanation.surface: An island that is very welcoming to hunters after game.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobago is the smaller island of the Caribbean nation Trinidad and Tobago.

clue.text: Exit path from Nansen's ship, heading for Pole

parts.note: of can mean from, as in 'a man of Kent'
the Fram was the ship the Norwegian explorer Fridtjof Nansen took into Arctic ice

indicators.note: only the first letter, the head, of the word is taken

parts.note: its first letter alone is taken, the head of the word

explanation.surface: A route off the polar explorer's ship as it heads for the Pole.
explanation.definitionFit: An off-ramp is a slip road for leaving a motorway or highway, a way out.

clue.text: Four without question recalled in this prefix?

indicators.note: what remains is called back, read in reverse
the question letters are removed

parts.note: a quartet is a group of four

explanation.surface: Four people recalled, without argument, to a word part.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the clue's first word: this is the prefix that means four.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetra- is the Greek-derived combining form meaning four, as in tetrahedron.

clue.text: Unknown figure in no way up for an award

indicators.note: in a down entry the word is written upwards

parts.note: not means no way, in no manner
in algebra y is an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: An anonymous person who will never be put up for a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tony is the annual American award for achievement in Broadway theatre.

clue.text: Bird book without much focus?

parts.note: rambling talk wanders aimlessly, without focus

explanation.surface: A meandering bird book with no real theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The brambling is a finch, a winter visitor to Britain closely related to the chaffinch.

clue.text: Resist American car disgorging one

indicators.note: the car spits out the letter for one

parts.note: Buick is a General Motors car brand

explanation.surface: A US car that refuses to go when a passenger is thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: To buck a trend or rule is to oppose or go against it.

clue.text: Dull and slimy when extracted

indicators.note: the letters for when are pulled out

parts.note: greasy means oily and slippery, so slimy
as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

explanation.surface: Something oily becomes lacklustre once it is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey describes something dreary and lacking colour or interest.

clue.text: Difficulty in conveying sensation aroused by eg a urinal

indicators.note: the letters are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: these nine letters are the fodder, rearranged

explanation.surface: Some sensation is stirred by a urinal, but there is trouble getting it across.
explanation.definitionFit: Neuralgia is intense pain along a nerve, a disorder of the nerves that carry sensation.

clue.text: Hunting opening for Holmes in investigation

indicators.note: the first letter of the name goes inside the case

parts.note: a case is an investigation

indicators.note: the opening letter of the detective's name

parts.note: the detective's name gives just its first letter

explanation.surface: A breakthrough for Sherlock Holmes in one of his inquiries.
explanation.definitionFit: The chase is the pursuit of game, the sport of hunting.
